dedupe_keys.name: yeti street level traffic emissions model

description: YETI, Yet Another Emissions From Traffic Inventory, is a Python tool for bottom-up road-traffic emissions calculation. It combines traffic activity with vehicle and pollutant factors under methods such as COPERT or HBEFA to build fine spatial inventories. Users supply a road network, vehicle activity, fleet composition and emission factors; outputs are street-level emissions by pollutant and time for the study area. Geographic coverage is user-defined, although factor methods have regional assumptions. GPL-3.0 source and Read the Docs guidance are public. The repository's last code push was in 2019, so current dependency compatibility and factor vintages need checking. A limitation is that activity or fleet errors can dominate the fine spatial output; it is not a measured roadside concentration. YETI can prepare air-quality inputs for transport-corridor and public-health simulations. The related catalogue ERA5 record provides weather, not traffic emissions. No traffic counts or package were downloaded.
inputs: Traffic, fleet and pollutant emission factors
name: YETI street-level traffic emissions model
